arch-deployment-unit-shapes.rationale: Keep deployment-unit diagrams and the distinction from instance count. Cross-module ACID is conditional on a shared transactional resource. Correct the questions so Shopify and Packwerk are not presented as complete enforcement of every code and data boundary. The deployment diagrams already compare the three structures directly.

arch-service-independence-costs.rationale: Required remote dependencies add latency and failure conditions; local calls also have failure modes. The independent availability product belongs in optional reference only. Journey connections map required dependencies and explicitly stop short of assuming independent failures. A familiar a journey with connections comparison makes the mechanism concrete; mapping and limits are explicit, with all required facts outside.

arch-team-capability-boundaries.rationale: Use capabilities, change locality and data ownership to diagnose boundaries. Replace an inexact attributed quotation with a paraphrase and remove the unnecessary compiler anecdote. Retain authoritative reservation rather than a stale local credit-limit check. The capability and team examples already supply concrete decision criteria.

arch-gradual-service-extraction.rationale: The extraction sequence correctly separates interfaces, migration, single write authority, catch-up and compatible rollback. Shared tables and lockstep releases diagnose coupling. Segment is an attributed historical example, not a universal migration prescription. The routing drawing and staged extraction example make the mechanism direct.

arch-replaceable-request-state.rationale: Replaceable instances may use disposable caches and working memory while required durable state lives elsewhere. Library-desk mapping explains replacement without hiding backing-store consistency or failure. No equation or additional analogy is needed. A familiar any library desk comparison makes the mechanism concrete; mapping and limits are explicit, with all required facts outside.

arch-session-store-token-tradeoffs.rationale: Review opaque sessions, signed-token integrity rather than secrecy, expiry, revocation and refresh-token tradeoffs. Key compromise and authorization changes still matter; self-contained tokens do not eliminate every server-side dependency. Revocation and expiry scenarios are clearer than a token metaphor.

arch-autoscaling-shared-bottlenecks.rationale: Scaling signals and measured startup delay precede arithmetic. Connection examples are full-pool bounds, not guaranteed active demand. Remove stranded formula-introduction prose and qualify pooler multiplexing by mode and transaction workload. The concrete connection-pool failure scenario exposes the shared bottleneck.

arch-pod-readiness-rollout-draining.rationale: Readiness routes traffic, liveness can restart a container, and startup probes delay other checks. Termination, hooks and endpoint updates race; surge and grace settings are not an unconditional availability guarantee. Actual stop-signal behavior was checked. Readiness, rolling replacement and draining are explicit operational steps.

arch-hpa-metric-stabilisation.rationale: CPU percentage is relative to requests. Keep the ceiling rule as optional reference and call its result a simplified recommendation before policies and limits. Missing metrics, readiness, tolerance and stabilization remain visible prerequisites. The controller’s observed-demand explanation is clearer than a second control metaphor.

arch-dynamic-endpoint-discovery.rationale: Client discovery and platform routing move selection to different places. DNS answers, caches, connection pools and endpoint updates have separate lifetimes. A stable service address does not make existing connections switch backends immediately. The two discovery drawings show who chooses an endpoint.

arch-mesh-traffic-policy-costs.rationale: Separate mesh traffic policy and workload identity from application correctness. Retries, timeouts, telemetry and sidecars carry costs; a mesh does not supply distributed transactions or make unsafe operations idempotent. The proxy diagram and cost discussion directly show the extra component.

arch-message-command-event-boundaries.rationale: Commands request action and events report facts; synchronous versus asynchronous is a separate dimension. Check outbox duplicates, saga compensation and schema ownership. Questions diagnose temporal coupling without claiming messaging removes all dependencies. Message/request examples distinguish intent and completion without metaphor.

arch-bounded-synchronous-dependencies.rationale: Deadlines, cancellation, bounded retries, jitter, circuit breakers and bulkheads each address a different failure path. Cancellation does not undo completed effects. Retry amplification was recomputed and idempotency remains a prerequisite. Request paths and deadlines already ground the failure mechanism.

arch-query-cost-replica-freshness.rationale: Execute the literal N+1 Python snippet with a recording adapter and verify 1,2,51 calls for 0,1,50 rows. Replica replay preserves the full write stream; route freshness-sensitive reads deliberately. Qualify the hypothetical 95% read example. The executable query loop and stale-read example make the problem tangible.

arch-cache-hit-load-freshness.rationale: The cache-first mixture and miss fraction are optional reference under a stated simple model. TTL, invalidation and origin load remain visible; the average does not predict tail latency or guarantee consistency. Independently enumerate hit/miss outcomes. Hit/miss examples directly distinguish speed, load and freshness.

arch-stored-read-model-maintenance.rationale: Correct unconditional join-cost and single-lookup wording. PostgreSQL refresh restrictions and ClickHouse insert-triggered incremental maintenance were checked. Projection versions, duplicates, lag and repair are visible outside the prepared-summary analogy. A familiar a prepared sales summary comparison makes the mechanism concrete; mapping and limits are explicit, with all required facts outside.

arch-precomputed-feeds-leaderboards.rationale: Compare fan-out cost at write and read time, including high-fanout users and read-time filtering. Redis sorted-set rank is zero-based and ordering semantics matter. Stored answers require maintenance rather than merely choosing a fast data structure. Feed and leaderboard examples already demonstrate precomputation.

arch-write-ownership-shard-routing.rationale: Shard routing should fit both queries and observed key popularity. Correct the worked example so many conversation IDs are not proof of balanced traffic, and distinguish time-bucket size control from splitting a current hot conversation. The router drawing and resharding consequences are concrete.

arch-batching-fixed-write-costs.rationale: Batching amortizes fixed overhead but increases delay, failure scope and resource use. Question reasoning is qualitative and preserves transaction/acknowledgment assumptions; batching is not automatically atomic or always faster. Batching’s fixed work and delay trade-off is direct.

arch-queue-burst-drain-budgets.rationale: A queue buys time for a finite burst only when later service exceeds arrivals. Check queue age, backlog, retention, retries and admitted work. Parcel-depot mapping explicitly denies infinite buffering and guaranteed completion time. A familiar a parcel depot comparison makes the mechanism concrete; mapping and limits are explicit, with all required facts outside.

arch-append-ledger-storage-tradeoffs.rationale: Append-oriented storage moves rather than removes work: WAL, memtables, flushes and compaction have distinct costs. Read/write amplification are not synonyms. Ledger appends still need invariant checks and retry-safe effects; no-overdraft does not follow from append-only storage. The ledger and storage-engine examples already expose the invariant risks.

arch-hot-key-write-mitigation.rationale: Salting expands key space but requires read aggregation; time buckets alone do not spread current hot-key writes. Numeric DynamoDB increments are not idempotent. Recompute capacity rounding and keep adaptive-splitting limitations visible. Salted-key routing is clearer as a small technical example.

arch-object-model-consistency-limits.rationale: Check current S3 strong object read/list semantics, conditional writes, versioning and object-lock limitations separately from multi-key transactions. Verify current 48.8TiB limit and per-prefix baseline rates without extending them to every provider or every bottleneck. Object/key and overwrite examples are familiar enough without a comparison.

arch-presigned-upload-version-safety.rationale: Presigned URLs are bounded bearer capabilities rather than one-use permissions. Validate expiry, temporary credentials, immutable identity, content checks and publish ordering. A later overwrite must not replace the object version that was inspected. The signed-upload sequence already shows transport and authority separately.

arch-multipart-part-size-recovery.rationale: Part count is optional planning reference. Recompute exact multiples, a short final part and the 10000-part limit. Current S3 limits, retries, completion, cleanup and non-MD5 multipart ETags remain visible without opening the formula. The multipart drawing directly shows independent retryable pieces.

arch-media-rendition-cdn-pipeline.rationale: Trace original storage, transcoding jobs, rendition publication, segments and CDN delivery. Safe retries and immutable publication matter independently of codec choice. ABR and compression benefits are conditional rather than guarantees. The rendition workflow directly maps stages and recovery.

arch-inverted-index-analysis-prefixes.rationale: Postings, Boolean combinations, tokenization and compatible analysis explain lexical matching.
